transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep losing a lot of time checking things over and over. Like locks, work files, revision notes, even my dressing supplies. I don’t really feel like I can move on until I’ve done the routine enough times that I calm down a bit.
Do you find yourself having repeated, intrusive thoughts or worries that you can’t control, which happen along with these checking behaviors?

Yeah… I do. It’s usually this thought that I missed one small thing. Like even if I know I cleaned the wound area, or checked a CAD file, it’ll still come in that maybe I missed something and it could cause an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. I try to tell myself it’s fine, but it doesn’t really go away.
Have these thoughts and checking behaviors been happening for most days over the past two weeks, and have they started to interfere with your work, relationships, or daily life?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s starting to mess things up.

At work, deadlines are slipping because I stay late checking things until I feel okay enough to send them. And I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups or workouts… the routines just take up that time now.

When you have these intrusive thoughts, do they almost always revolve around a fear of harm coming from something you might have missed, like an infection from an unclean wound or a mistake in a design file?

Yeah… mostly. It’s that I missed some tiny thing, even after I know I checked it. Like with cleaning the wound or reviewing a CAD file — my head keeps going, what if that one thing turns into an infection or someone gets hurt. I can’t really talk myself out of it.
